passage: At the small insurance office in Nanded, Abhinav noticed on Monday that his teammate Wasim had typed the wrong policy number on a client's renewal papers. It would take five minutes to fix. But Wasim was already stressed, and Abhinav hated awkward talks. "I'll tell him tomorrow," he thought. Tuesday passed. Wednesday passed. The papers went out with the other files. On Friday the client called, angry: his payment had gone to the wrong account, and he had to visit the office twice to sort it. The manager called both of them in. Wasim looked at Abhinav. "You saw it on Monday?" Abhinav nodded, unable to look up. What would have been a quiet word had become a meeting with the manager and a client complaint.

qa.q: When did Abhinav notice the wrong policy number?
What was Abhinav feeling when Wasim asked, 'You saw it on Monday?'
qa.a: He felt ashamed and guilty, unable to look up, knowing a small fix had become a big problem.

qa.q: What went wrong, and what could fix it next time?
qa.a: Abhinav avoided an awkward talk; a quiet word on Monday, while it was a five-minute fix, would have spared everyone.

qa.q: How does Wasim experience finding out?
qa.a: Wasim likely feels hurt and let down that a teammate saw the mistake and said nothing for days.

grounding: A colleague delays telling a teammate about a mistake until the client notices, and the talk becomes harder.

subtype: Approach: avoids a difficult conversation and lets the problem grow [Pitfall]
passage: In the marketing agency in Milan, Valentina spotted the problem on Tuesday morning: in the brochure her teammate Ada had designed, the shop's phone number had two digits swapped. Ada was proud of the brochure; she'd worked on it for weeks. Valentina thought, "I'll find a good moment." The good moment didn't come. On Thursday the brochure went to print, five thousand copies. On Monday the client called. Customers had been ringing a stranger all weekend. The client was furious and asked for a reprint at the agency's cost. Ada turned to Valentina in the corridor. "Did you know?" Valentina said, "Since Tuesday." Ada's face went pale. The conversation Valentina had avoided had become far worse.

qa.q: How many copies went to print?
Why did Valentina keep putting off telling Ada?
qa.a: She felt uncomfortable criticising work Ada was proud of, and kept waiting for a good moment that never came.

qa.q: What would you change first if you were Valentina on Tuesday?
qa.a: Tell Ada quietly that day, kindly and simply, while it was an easy fix before printing.

qa.q: How did Ada feel when she heard 'Since Tuesday'?
qa.a: Ada felt shocked and hurt; her face went pale at knowing a teammate had seen it days earlier.

grounding: A colleague delays telling a teammate about a mistake until the client notices, and the conversation becomes harder.
